verses.text: Some time later, Amnon son of David fell in love with Tamar. She was the beautiful sister of Absalom, another son of David.
Amnon wanted her so much that he made himself sick over his sister Tamar. She was a virgin, and it seemed impossible for Amnon to do anything to her.
But Amnon had a friend named Jonadab, the son of David's brother Shimeah. Jonadab was a very clever and cunning man.
He asked Amnon, "You are the king's son. Why do you look so miserable every morning? Won't you tell me?" Amnon said to him, "I am in love with Tamar, my brother Absalom's sister."

Jonadab said to him, "Lie down on your bed and pretend to be sick. When your father comes to see you, say to him, 'Please let my sister Tamar come and give me something to eat. Let her make the food in front of me, so I can watch her and eat it from her hand.'"

So Amnon lay down and pretended to be sick. When the king came to see him, Amnon said to him, "Please let my sister Tamar come and make a couple of special cakes in front of me, so I can eat them from her hand."
So David sent a message to Tamar at the palace: "Please go to your brother Amnon's house and make some food for him."
So Tamar went to her brother Amnon's house, where he was lying down. She took some dough, kneaded it, made cakes while he watched, and baked them.
Then she took the pan and served him the cakes, but he refused to eat. Amnon said, "Send everyone out of here." So everyone went out.
Then Amnon said to Tamar, "Bring the food into my bedroom so I can eat from your hand." Tamar took the cakes she had made and brought them to her brother Amnon in the bedroom.
But when she held them out for him to eat, he grabbed her and said, "Come to bed with me, my sister!"
She said to him, "No, my brother! Don't force me! Such a thing should never be done in Israel. Don't do this shameful thing!
Where could I go with my shame? And you would be like one of the worst fools in Israel. Please, just speak to the king. He will not stop you from marrying me."
But he would not listen to her. He was stronger than she was, so he forced her and raped her.
Then Amnon hated her very much. He hated her even more than he had loved her before. Amnon said to her, "Get up and get out!"
She said to him, "No! Sending me away now is an even greater wrong than what you have already done to me!" But he would not listen to her.
He called his personal servant and said, "Get this woman out of my sight, and lock the door behind her."
She was wearing a long robe with sleeves, because that is what the king's unmarried daughters wore. So his servant put her out and locked the door behind her.
Tamar put ashes on her head and tore the long robe she was wearing. She put her hand on her head and went away, crying loudly as she went.

Her brother Absalom said to her, "Has your brother Amnon been with you? For now, my sister, keep quiet about it. He is your brother. Don't let this break your heart." So Tamar lived in her brother Absalom's house, lonely and sad.
When King David heard about all this, he was very angry.
Absalom did not say a word to Amnon, good or bad. He hated Amnon because Amnon had raped his sister Tamar.
Two full years later, Absalom's sheep were being sheared at Baal Hazor, near Ephraim, and Absalom invited all the king's sons to come.
Absalom went to the king and said, "My sheep are being sheared. Will the king and his officials please come and join me?"
The king answered Absalom, "No, my son. We should not all go. We would only be a burden to you." Absalom kept urging him, but the king still would not go. Instead, he gave Absalom his blessing.
Then Absalom said, "If you won't come, then please let my brother Amnon come with us." The king asked him, "Why should he go with you?"
But Absalom kept urging him, so the king let Amnon and all his other sons go with Absalom.

Absalom ordered his servants, "Watch Amnon. When he is happy from drinking wine and I say to you, 'Strike Amnon,' then kill him. Don't be afraid. I am the one giving you this order. Be strong and brave!"
So Absalom's servants did to Amnon what Absalom had ordered. Then all the king's other sons got up, jumped on their mules, and ran away.
While they were still on the way, a report came to David: "Absalom has killed all the king's sons. Not one of them is left!"
The king stood up, tore his clothes, and lay down on the ground. All his servants stood beside him with their clothes torn too.

But Jonadab, the son of David's brother Shimeah, said, "My lord, don't think they have killed all the young princes, the king's sons. Only Amnon is dead. Absalom has been planning this ever since the day Amnon raped his sister Tamar.
So, my lord the king, don't believe that all your sons are dead. Only Amnon is dead."
Meanwhile, Absalom ran away. Then the young man who was keeping watch looked up and saw many people coming down the road along the hillside behind him.
Jonadab said to the king, "Look, the king's sons are coming! It is just as your servant said."
As soon as he finished speaking, the king's sons arrived, crying loudly. The king and all his servants also cried very hard.
But Absalom ran away and went to Talmai son of Ammihud, the king of Geshur. And David mourned for his son every day.
After Absalom ran away to Geshur, he stayed there for three years.
King David's heart longed to go out to Absalom, because he had got over the death of Amnon.
